allLanesRejected.question: A girl cycling east at 5 km/h sees the rain falling vertically. At 20 km/h, the rain appears to fall at 60° to the vertical, hitting her from the front. Find the actual speed of the rain, the angle it makes with the vertical, and which side it is tilted toward.
planContents: {"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","subject":"physics","question":"A girl cycling east at 5 km/h sees the rain falling vertically. At 20 km/h, the rain appears to fall at 60° to the vertical, hitting her from the front. Find the actual speed of the rain, the angle it makes with the vertical, and which side it is tilted toward.","givens":[{"id":"v1","symbol":"v_g1","value":5,"unit":"km/h","sourceText":"cycling east at 5 km/h","provenance":"given"},{"id":"v2","symbol":"v_g2","value":20,"unit":"km/h","sourceText":"At 20 km/h","provenance":"given"},{"id":"a2","symbol":"theta_app","value":60,"unit":"deg","sourceText":"appears to fall at 60° to the vertical","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"vr","symbol":"v_r","unit":"km/h"},{"id":"ang","symbol":"theta","unit":"deg"},{"id":"side","symbol":"tilt_side"}],"derived":[{"id":"vx","symbol":"v_rx","value":5,"unit":"km/h","sign":"+","sourceText":"v_rx = 5 km/h (eastward component of rain velocity)","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["v1"]},{"id":"vy","symbol":"v_ry","value":15,"unit":"km/h","sign":"-","sourceText":"tan60 = (20-5)/|v_ry| => |v_ry| = 15/tan60 = 15/1.732 = 8.66; check: sqrt(25+75)=10","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["v2","a2","vx"]},{"id":"vr","symbol":"v_r","value":10,"unit":"km/h","sign":"+","sourceText":"v_r = sqrt(5^2 + (15/sqrt3)^2) = sqrt(25+75) = sqrt(100) = 10","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["vx","vy"]},{"id":"ang","symbol":"theta","value":30,"unit":"deg","sign":"+","sourceText":"tan(theta) = v_rx/|v_ry| = 5/(15/sqrt3) = sqrt3/3 => theta = 30","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["vx","vy"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"When the girl rides east at 5 km/h the rain appears vertical, so the rain's horizontal component equals her velocity: rain moves eastward at 5 km/h.","expected":"v_rx = +5 km/h east","relatedQuantityIds":["v1","vx"]},{"id":"c2","claim":"At 20 km/h east, the relative horizontal wind is 20-5 = 15 km/h from the front (westward in her frame); with apparent angle 60° from vertical, vertical component = 15/tan60 = 5*sqrt3 ≈ 8.66 km/h downward.","expected":"|v_ry| = 15/tan(60°) = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 km/h","relatedQuantityIds":["v2","a2","vy"]},{"id":"c3","claim":"Actual rain speed combines components: sqrt(5^2 + (5√3)^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 km/h.","expected":"v_r = 10 km/h","relatedQuantityIds":["vr","vx","vy"]},{"id":"c4","claim":"True angle from vertical: tan(theta) = 5/(5√3) = 1/√3, so theta = 30°.","expected":"theta = 30° to the vertical","relatedQuantityIds":["ang","vx","vy"]},{"id":"c5","claim":"Since the rain's horizontal component is eastward (same direction as her motion) and it hits her from the front as she rides east, the rain is tilted toward the east, i.e., toward the direction she cycles / coming from the west behind her overhead and striking her front.","expected":"tilted toward the east (direction of motion), hitting her front","relatedQuantityIds":["side","vx"]}],"lawIds":["relative_velocity_vector_subtraction","velocity_components_trigonometry","pythagorean_magnitude","tangent_angle_relation"],"assumptions":["Rain velocity is constant and uniform (same in both observations).","Girl cycles due east in both cases; east taken as +x, downward as -y.","Apparent direction of rain is the direction of the relative velocity of rain with respect to the girl.","Angles measured from the vertical (downward) direction.","No wind changes between the two observations."],"visualRequirement":"optional"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","subject":"physics","question":"A girl cycling east at 5 km/h sees the rain falling vertically. At 20 km/h, the rain appears to fall at 60° to the vertical, hitting her from the front. Find the actual speed of the rain, the angle it makes with the vertical, and which side it is tilted toward.","givens":[{"id":"v1","symbol":"v_g1","value":5,"unit":"km/h","sourceText":"cycling east at 5 km/h","provenance":"given"},{"id":"v2","symbol":"v_g2","value":20,"unit":"km/h","sourceText":"At 20 km/h","provenance":"given"},{"id":"a2","symbol":"theta_app2","value":60,"unit":"deg","sourceText":"appears to fall at 60° to the vertical","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"vr","symbol":"v_r","unit":"km/h"},{"id":"ang","symbol":"theta","unit":"deg"},{"id":"side","symbol":"tilt_direction"}],"derived":[{"id":"vy","symbol":"v_ry","value":5,"unit":"km/h","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["v1"],"sourceText":"vertical component of rain velocity equals 5 km/h from first observation"},{"id":"vx","symbol":"v_rx","value":-8.66,"unit":"km/h","sign":"negative","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["v2","a2","vy"],"sourceText":"horizontal component: tan60 = (20 - v_rx)/5 gives v_rx = 20 - 5√3 ≈ 11.34? recompute: apparent angle tan60=(v_g2 - v_rx)/v_ry → v_rx = 20 - 5·tan60 = 20 - 8.66 = 11.34 east; but rain hits from front so tilted toward her, i.e., from east, horizontal component westward: v_rx = 20 - 5√3? Actually apparent horizontal = v_rx - v_g2; |v_rx - 20| = 5√3 = 8.66, hitting from front means rain comes from ahead (east), so v_rx > 20? No: rain tilted toward east means it moves westward relative... v_rx = 20 + 8.66 = 28.66? Standard answer: rain speed 10 km/h at 30° to vertical tilted toward east (toward the girl). Recompute: v_ry = 5, tanθ = v_rx/v_ry; apparent at 20: tan60 = (v_rx - 20)/5 if rain moves east faster... v_rx = 20 + 8.66 = 28.66 gives speed ~29.1. Alternative: rain horizontal component toward west (toward girl's face from front-east means rain moves westward): v_rx = -x; apparent horizontal = -x - 20, magnitude x+20 = 5√3 → x = -11.34, speed = √(25+128.6)=12.4. Hmm. Standard problem: answer v_r = 10 km/h, 30° to vertical. Check: v_rx = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 east, v_ry = 5. At 5 km/h east: relative horizontal = 8.66-5 = 3.66 ≠ 0. So not vertical. Try v_rx = 5: then at 5 km/h relative horizontal = 0 ✓. At 20: relative horizontal = 5-20 = -15, tan = 15/v_ry = tan60 → v_ry = 15/√3 = 5√3 ≈ 8.66. Speed = √(25+75) = 10 km/h ✓. Angle: tanθ = 5/(5√3) = 1/√3 → θ = 30° ✓. Direction: rain moves eastward horizontally (same direction as girl) but slower; apparent rain comes from front (east) tilted toward the east, i.e., tilted toward the girl's direction of motion / from the front-east. So v_rx = +5 east, v_ry = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 downward."},{"id":"vr_ans","symbol":"v_r","value":10,"unit":"km/h","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["vx","vy"],"sourceText":"v_r = √(5² + (5√3)²) = √(25+75) = √100 = 10 km/h"},{"id":"ang_ans","symbol":"theta","value":30,"unit":"deg","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["vx","vy"],"sourceText":"tanθ = 5/(5√3) = 1/√3 → θ = 30° to the vertical"}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"When the girl cycles east at 5 km/h the rain appears vertical, so the rain's horizontal (eastward) component equals her speed: v_rx = 5 km/h east.","expected":"v_rx = 5 km/h east","relatedQuantityIds":["v1","vx"]},{"id":"c2","claim":"At 20 km/h east, the relative horizontal velocity of rain is 5 − 20 = −15 km/h (toward her from the front), and tan60° = 15/v_ry gives v_ry = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 km/h downward.","expected":"v_ry = 15/tan60° = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 km/h","relatedQuantityIds":["v2","a2","vy"]},{"id":"c3","claim":"Actual rain speed is 10 km/h.","expected":"v_r = √(5² + (5√3)²) = 10 km/h","relatedQuantityIds":["vr_ans","vr"]},{"id":"c4","claim":"Rain makes 30° with the vertical.","expected":"θ = arctan(1/√3) = 30°","relatedQuantityIds":["ang_ans","ang"]},{"id":"c5","claim":"The rain is tilted toward the east — the same direction the girl rides — so as she speeds up it appears to slant and hit her from the front.","expected":"tilted toward the east (direction of motion), striking her from the front","relatedQuantityIds":["side","vx"]}],"lawIds":["relative_velocity","vector_addition","trigonometry_tangent"],"assumptions":["Rain velocity is constant and uniform","East is the positive horizontal direction; vertical component is downward","Apparent direction is the relative velocity of rain with respect to the girl","Speeds are exact, angles measured from vertical"],"visualRequirement":"optional"}
